status: CPU native selector and complete kernel compiled; GPU trial not yet submitted
purpose: Screen local-expert kernels before implementing PP4/EAGLE/NIXL integration. This is not an end-to-end serving result.
control: Current optimized EP4,4x4001 tokens,140 physical experts
candidate: Four independent EP1 groups,8002 tokens each,128 logical experts; divide per-GPU kernel time by2 for equal per-request work budget.
platform: Firmus H200, one node, four active GPUs; replaces ASPIRE by explicit user instruction
weights: Deterministic synthetic FP8 weights and original FP32 block scales, same per logical expert in both configurations. Captured production routing only; not actual model weights or an output-quality evaluation.

fixture.selection: p10,p50,p90 held-out remote FC2 fraction across94 layers; no candidate timings used.

numeric_gate: Compare all live outputs against unchanged EP4 math with matching weights, inputs and topk weights; sampled independent FP32 reference; changed-input repeats and masked tails.
timing_protocol: Same four GPUs; interleaved EP4/local order, cache eviction before timed interval, rank maximum, normalized local time/2; retain raw samples and clocks.
performance_gate: At least15% lower normalized time in every selected layer and both source captures, with paired p90<1 and control drift<=5%. This justifies integration work, not a predicted serving score or ASPIRE6500 result.

cpu_validation.toolchain: CUDA13.0.88, complete SM90a native kernel; no GPU execution

remaining: Build a fresh image with opt-in local EP1 host selection.
Run numerical and normalized latency PoC on the authorized single H200 node.
Only if promising: implement PP auxiliary state forwarding, draft handling, scheduling and KV lifetime/transfer; validate ordinary serving. Kernel PoC is not a serving score.
reason_for_measurement: Existing data cannot determine whether eliminating remote dispatch/scatter and inter-rank barriers outweighs larger expert weight footprint, changed padding and local combine costs. The PoC tests the net local-kernel cost, not isolated NVLink bandwidth.
